concepts.name: Establishment and Statutory Basis of FCI
key_dimensions: FCI established under Food Corporations Act, 1964 (not a constitutional body)
Distinction from NAFED, CCI, and other procurement agencies — FCI is the nodal agency
Ownership structure: Government of India enterprise under Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
Year of operationalization (1965) vs. year of Act (1964) — a common UPSC trap

concepts.name: Minimum Support Price (MSP) and FCI's Procurement Role
key_dimensions: FCI as the primary agency for MSP-based procurement of wheat and rice (not all 23 MSP crops)
Distinction: FCI procures wheat and rice directly; other crops handled by NAFED, state agencies
Price Support Scheme (PSS) vs. Market Intervention Scheme (MIS) — FCI's role in each
Decentralized Procurement Scheme (DCP): states procure on FCI's behalf — implications for cost and efficiency

concepts.name: Central Pool and Buffer Stock Norms
key_dimensions: Central Pool: aggregate of foodgrains held by FCI + state agencies for food security operations
Buffer stock norms vs. strategic reserve — difference and who decides the norms (DOCA)
Quarterly buffer norms (April 1, July 1, October 1, January 1) — norms differ by quarter
Excess stock beyond buffer norms: implications for open market sale (OMSS) and fiscal burden

concepts.name: Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) and FCI's Supply Chain Role
key_dimensions: FCI's role: procurement → storage → transportation to state depots (last-mile by states)
Distinction between FCI's role and state governments' role in TPDS — a frequent exam overlap
National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013: FCI's obligations under NFSA vs. earlier TPDS framework
Subsidized grain allocation: AAY (Antyodaya Anna Yojana) vs. Priority Household categories — FCI supplies both

concepts.name: Food Subsidy and Economic Cost of FCI Operations
key_dimensions: Economic cost = procurement cost + storage & handling + distribution charges (not just MSP)
Central Issue Price (CIP) vs. Economic Cost — the gap constitutes food subsidy paid to FCI
Food subsidy routed through FCI vs. DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) debates
NFSA mandates heavily subsidized prices (₹1/2/3 per kg) — fiscal implications and PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana overlay

concepts.name: Shanta Kumar Committee Recommendations on FCI Restructuring
key_dimensions: Key recommendations: restrict FCI to wheat/rice procurement, hand over other crops to state agencies
Suggested reduction of NFSA coverage from ~67% to 40% of population
End-to-end computerization and introduction of cash transfers instead of physical grain distribution
Liquidation of excess stocks via OMSS and export — recommendation vs. actual government action (contrast)

concepts.name: Decentralized Procurement Scheme (DCP)
key_dimensions: Under DCP, state governments procure, store, and distribute foodgrains — FCI reimburses costs
States currently under DCP vs. states where FCI directly procures — distinction important
Advantages: reduced transportation cost, better local variety procurement, lower spoilage
Accountability gap: state-level procurement irregularities harder to monitor under DCP

concepts.name: FCI's Storage Infrastructure and Capacity Challenges
key_dimensions: Types of storage: CAP (Cover and Plinth) vs. scientific storage (silos, warehouses) — FCI mostly uses conventional
Private warehousing under Negotiable Warehouse Receipts (NWR) system — FCI's limited use
Grain wastage and storage losses: CAG reports on FCI's storage inefficiencies
Silo-based storage policy: FCI's shift toward steel silos under PPP mode — current status

concepts.name: Open Market Sale Scheme (OMSS) by FCI
key_dimensions: Purpose: offload excess buffer stock to cool domestic food price inflation
Domestic OMSS vs. export of foodgrains — different policy triggers and approvals required
Controversy: states' demand to include OMSS grain in PDS vs. Centre's position on separate channels
Recent suspension of OMSS to states (2023) and its implications for state-run welfare schemes

concepts.name: National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013 and FCI's Obligations
key_dimensions: NFSA coverage: 75% rural + 50% urban population (approx. 67% total) — legally enforceable entitlements
FCI's duty to ensure adequate allocation to states — legal liability vs. earlier welfare scheme approach
PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY): free grain distribution merged into NFSA from Jan 2023 — FCI operational implications
Grievance redressal under NFSA: District Grievance Redressal Officer — FCI's indirect accountability

concepts.name: Price Stabilization and FCI's Role in Inflation Management
key_dimensions: FCI buffer stock as a tool to moderate food inflation — mechanism of release into open market
Distinction: FCI manages cereals (wheat/rice); vegetables managed by Price Stabilization Fund (PSF) under different ministry
Wheat and rice CPI vs. FCI stock levels — correlation and policy debates
WTO Agreement on Agriculture: public stockholding for food security — India's negotiating position defended by FCI operations

concepts.name: WTO and Public Stockholding Programme — FCI at the Centre of Controversy
key_dimensions: WTO's Aggregate Measurement of Support (AMS): cap on domestic support at 10% of value of production for developing countries
India's argument: MSP-based procurement by FCI is food security, not trade-distorting subsidy
Bali Peace Clause (2013) and Nairobi Ministerial (2015): interim protection for India's public stockholding
Demand for permanent solution at WTO — FCI's procurement volumes as the core contentious data

concepts.name: FCI's Financial Health and Borrowings from NSSF
key_dimensions: FCI borrows from National Small Savings Fund (NSSF) to bridge gap between food subsidy released and actual requirement
Off-balance-sheet financing of food subsidy: implications for fiscal deficit calculations (a UPSC trap)
CAG observations on FCI's growing debt and interest burden
Budget 2021-22 onwards: government moved toward full upfront budgetary support to FCI, ending NSSF borrowings

concepts.name: Relationship Between FCI, State Agencies, and CWC/SWC in Foodgrain Management
key_dimensions: Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC) vs. State Warehousing Corporations (SWC) vs. FCI: storage hierarchy
FCI hires storage space from CWC and SWC — ownership vs. operational control distinction
WDRA (Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority): regulates warehouses but not FCI directly
Coordination failure: multiple agencies handling storage leading to accountability gaps highlighted by CAG

concepts.name: Procurement Concentration and Regional Imbalance in FCI Operations
key_dimensions: Over 80% of wheat procurement from Punjab, Haryana, MP; rice from Punjab, Haryana, AP, Telangana, Chhattisgarh
Why northeastern and eastern states are underrepresented: infrastructure, APMC laws, awareness — exam-relevant analysis
Farmer distress in non-procuring states despite MSP announcement — policy gap
Attempts to expand procurement: PM-AASHA scheme and its limited success in replacing FCI in non-cereal procurement

concepts.name: FCI and Digitization: e-Procurement, ANNAVITRAN, and ONE NATION ONE RATION CARD
key_dimensions: ANNAVITRAN portal: tracks real-time allocation and lifting of foodgrains by states from FCI
One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC): portability of PDS entitlements — FCI's backend supply role unchanged
e-Procurement and online auction for OMSS: transparency improvements
Aadhaar-seeding of beneficiaries vs. FCI's role — distinction between identity verification (states) and supply (FCI)

concepts.name: FCI's Role in Export of Foodgrains
key_dimensions: FCI can export surplus foodgrains when domestic stocks exceed buffer norms — requires Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approval
India's rice and wheat export bans (2022–23): FCI stock data used to justify export restrictions
Conflict between export earnings and domestic food security — policy tension
FCI does not export directly; tenders are issued — distinction from operational export agencies

concepts.name: Fortified Rice Distribution through FCI
key_dimensions: Government mandate to distribute fortified rice (iron, folic acid, Vitamin B12) through PDS by 2024
FCI's role: procure fortified rice from millers, blend with normal rice at 1:100 ratio
Challenges: cost implications, miller capacity, consumer awareness and acceptance
Distinction: fortification is a value-addition mandate on FCI, not part of original procurement mandate — institutional stretch

concepts.name: Millet/Coarse Cereal Procurement and FCI's Expanding Mandate
key_dimensions: International Year of Millets 2023: push to include millets in PDS — FCI's limited infrastructure for millets
Odisha's millet mission vs. FCI's cereal-centric procurement structure — state vs. central agency contrast
NAFED vs. FCI: who handles millet procurement under PSS — important distinction for MCQs
FCI's mandate traditionally wheat and rice — expanding to millets requires legislative/policy amendment debate

concepts.name: Accountability and Oversight Mechanisms for FCI
key_dimensions: Parliamentary oversight: FCI is a PSU — subject to CAG audit, Parliamentary Standing Committee scrutiny
CAG's recurring findings: stock discrepancies, storage losses, overpayment to transporters
FCI not under RTI directly but as a public authority is covered — nuance on information disclosure
Internal vigilance vs. CBI investigations in procurement irregularities — governance dimension
